We need retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to find templates for disconnections. The target: a sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings, plus an amide attached to a trans-alkene (styryl amide). Structure: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring bearing trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Actually Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So a tolyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring that has a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 (anilide with an aniline at the amide nitrogen). So we can think retrosynthesis: disconnection of sulfonamide (sulfonyl chloride + amine). Also disconnection of amide (acid chloride + amine). Also disconnection of alkene (maybe Wittig or Heck). But limited to 3 steps.

Potential route: Step1: Form sulfonamide by reacting p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) with an aniline that already contains the rest of molecule (the phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). So we need that aniline: 4-(... )-aniline? Actually the sulfonamide attaches to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) at para position relative to the alkene side chain? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl via N (NS(=O)(=O) attached to that phenyl). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) as substituent, not the aniline. Wait: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2 means the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) as a substituent (the N is attached to the sulfonyl group and to the first phenyl (tolyl) as part of sulfonamide? Actually NS(=O)(=O)c2... means N attached to sulfonyl and to the first phenyl? The SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2)cc1. So the N is attached to the first phenyl (tolyl) as substituent (anilide). The sulfonyl group attaches to the second phenyl (c2...). So it's a sulfonamide linking two phenyls: tolyl-N-SO2-Ph-... So the N is attached to tolyl, the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl.

Thus we can disconnect sulfonamide: tolyl amine (p-toluidine) + sulfonyl chloride derived from second phenyl with side chain (aryl sulfonyl chloride). So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride: 4-(... )-phenylsulfonyl chloride. That can be made from the corresponding phenyl with side chain via chlorosulfonation (SO2Cl). Might be expensive.

Alternative: disconnection at amide: we can form amide between the side chain carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So we need an acid (or acid chloride) with the alkene side chain, and aniline.

Thus route: Step1: Synthesize the acid (or acid chloride) containing the trans-alkene attached to phenyl (the second phenyl). That could be from cinnamic acid derivative (trans-4-...?). Actually the side chain is /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 attached to phenyl. So we need 4-(trans-... )-benzoic acid? The phenyl ring (c2) has a para substituent of the alkene amide. So we need 4-(trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2)benzenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl chloride attaches to that phenyl at the position where the side chain is attached? The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl via S(=O)(=O) to that phenyl (the sulfonyl attached to the phenyl at the position where the side chain is attached? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl at the same carbon as the side chain? The SMILES: S(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/... )cc2. So the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl at the position where the side chain is also attached? No, the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl at the carbon bearing the side chain? The phenyl has two substituents: the sulfonyl group attached to the phenyl (as a substituent) and the side chain (alkene amide) attached also to the phenyl. So the phenyl is disubstituted (para? maybe meta). So we need a di-substituted phenyl.

Thus maybe better to start from commercially available 4-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride (p-aminobenzenesulfonyl chloride) and then do sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine? But we need the phenyl with side chain, not amine.

Alternative: Use Suzuki coupling to attach side chain onto sulfonyl phenyl after sulfonamide formation.

Given limited steps, maybe we can propose a route using three steps: 1) Form amide between trans-cinnamic acid (commercial) and aniline (commercial) to give trans-cinnamoyl anilide (C6H5-CO-CH=CH-Ph-NH2?). Actually trans-cinnamic acid + aniline gives trans-cinnamoyl aniline (Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph). That's close but we need extra NH2 on the aniline (the aniline is 4-aminophenyl? Actually the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl with NH2 (aniline). So we need 4-aminophenyl amide. So we need 4-aminophenyl as amine, reacting with trans-cinnamic acid chloride to give trans-cinnamoyl-4-aminophenyl (Ph-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2). That's exactly the side chain.

So step1: Convert trans-cinnamic acid to acid chloride (using SOCl2) (maybe not needed if using coupling reagent). But we can use standard amide formation with coupling reagent, but for retrosynthesis we can consider amide formation as a step.

Thus precursor A: trans-cinnamic acid (commercial). Precursor B: 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) (commercial). Reaction: amide coupling to give side chain product (call it intermediate I).

Step2: Sulfonylation: we need to attach sulfonyl group to the phenyl of intermediate I (the phenyl bearing the side chain). The sulfonyl group is attached to the phenyl via sulfonyl chloride derived from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl attaches to the phenyl and the nitrogen of sulfonamide attaches to p-toluidine. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) reacting with the aniline of intermediate I? Wait the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl (the N is attached to p-tolyl). So we need p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) as nucleophile, reacting with aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from the phenyl of intermediate I (which has side chain). So we need to convert that phenyl (with side chain) into sulfonyl chloride (i.e., chlorosulfonation). That may be not commercially available.

Alternative: Use p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) reacting with the aniline of intermediate I (the aniline is the NH2 on the phenyl attached to amide). That would give sulfonamide linking p-tolyl sulfonyl to the aniline nitrogen, but the target has sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to the phenyl (the N attached to p-tolyl). Actually the target N is attached to p-tolyl, not to the side chain phenyl. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to p-tolyl, and the sulfonyl attached to the phenyl with side chain. So the sulfonamide nitrogen is part of p-toluidine (p-tolyl-NH-). So we need p-toluidine reacting with sulfonyl chloride derived from the side-chain phenyl. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl = phenyl with side chain). That may not be commercially available.

Maybe alternative disconnection: form sulfonamide first using p-toluenesulfonyl chloride and p-toluidine? Not correct.

Given constraints, perhaps we can propose a 3-step route using commercially available building blocks: 1) Start from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) and 4-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine) to make p-tolyl-sulfonamide attached to phenyl with NH2 (i.e., p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph-NH2). That's a sulfonamide intermediate. Then step2: acylate the remaining NH2 with trans-cinnamoyl chloride to give the final product. That would give N-sulfonyl-N'-acyl? But the target has the sulfonamide nitrogen attached to p-tolyl, and the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl (the same phenyl). In our intermediate, the phenyl has NH2 (attached to sulfonyl). After acylation, the NH2 becomes amide with trans-cinnamoyl, giving the correct connectivity: p-tolyl-NH-SO2-Ph-NH-CO-CH=CH-Ph. However the target has the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl and also has an extra NH2 on that phenyl? Wait target: ...C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N. That is amide attached to an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 para to the amide? Actually the SMILES: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N means the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which also has an NH2 at some position (maybe para). So the phenyl has both the amide and an NH2 substituent. In our intermediate, the phenyl after sulfonamide has only one NH2 (the one that will be acylated). After acylation, that NH becomes amide, leaving no free NH2. But target requires an additional NH2 on that phenyl (maybe at para). So our route missing that extra NH2.

Thus we need phenyl with two substituents: one sulfonyl (attached via sulfonyl group) and one amide, plus an NH2 elsewhere. Actually the phenyl in target has side chain (alkene amide) and also is attached to sulfonyl group (via sulfonyl). The amide nitrogen attaches to another phenyl that has an NH2 (the c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to a phenyl that has an NH2 substituent (an aniline). So the amide is between the side chain carbonyl and an aniline (para-aminophenyl). So the phenyl bearing the side chain is not the same as the phenyl bearing the NH2. So we have two phenyl rings: phenyl A (attached to sulfonyl and side chain) and phenyl B (attached to amide nitrogen and has NH2). So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl B, which also has NH2 (maybe para). So we need phenyl B = p-aminophenyl (4-aminophenyl). So the amide is formed between side chain carbonyl and p-aminophenyl (aniline). That's fine.

Thus our earlier step: trans-cinnamic acid + p-aminophenyl (p-phenylenediamine? Actually p-aminophenyl is aniline with NH2 at para? That's just aniline? Wait aniline is phenyl-NH2. p-aminophenyl would be phenyl with NH2 at para relative to something else, but if it's just the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl, the phenyl has an NH2 substituent elsewhere. So the amide nitrogen is attached to phenyl at position 1, and the phenyl also has NH2 at position 4. So the building block is 4-aminophenylamine? That's p-phenylenediamine (1,4-diaminobenzene). Indeed p-phenylenediamine has two NH2 groups para. One can be used for amide formation, the other remains free. So we can use p-phenylenediamine as the amine for amide coupling with trans-cinnamic acid to give trans-cinnamoyl-p-phenylenediamine (one amide, one free NH2). That matches the side chain part.

Thus step1: trans-cinnamic acid + p-phenylenediamine -> amide (using coupling reagent). Product: intermediate I: trans-cinnamoyl-p-phenylenediamine (one NH2 free). This matches the side chain attached to phenyl B.

Step2: Sulfonylation: we need to attach sulfonyl group to the free NH2 of intermediate I, using p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl). That will give sulfonamide linking p-tolyl to the phenyl B (which is the same phenyl as the amide). However target has sulfonyl attached to phenyl A, not phenyl B. Wait the sulfonyl is attached to phenyl A (the phenyl that is attached to the side chain). In our intermediate, the free NH2 is on phenyl B (the same phenyl that has amide). So sulfonyl would be attached to phenyl B, not correct.

Thus we need sulfonyl attached to phenyl A, which is the phenyl bearing the side chain (the trans-alkene). That phenyl currently is part of the trans-cinnamic acid (the acid's phenyl). In trans-cinnamic acid, the phenyl is attached to the alkene carbonyl. So after amide formation, the phenyl A is part of the amide carbonyl side chain (the phenyl attached to carbonyl). That phenyl does not have any NH2. So we cannot sulfonylate it directly. We need to attach sulfonyl to that phenyl via electrophilic aromatic substitution (sulfonyl chloride) onto the phenyl ring (which is possible if we have a sulfonyl chloride that reacts with aromatic ring? Typically sulfonylation of aromatic rings uses sulfonyl chloride with a Lewis acid to give sulfonyl aryl (aryl sulfone), not sulfonamide. But target is sulfonamide linking phenyl A via sulfonyl group to N of p-tolyl. So we need aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from phenyl A (with side chain) reacting with p-toluidine. That seems more plausible.

Thus we need to generate aryl sulfonyl chloride from phenyl A (which has side chain). That could be done via chlorosulfonation of phenyl A (introducing SO2Cl group). That is a step. So step2: chlorosulfonation of phenyl A (the trans-cinnamoyl phenyl) to give aryl sulfonyl chloride (Ar-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2? Wait the sulfonyl chloride would be on the phenyl ring, not interfering with amide). Then step3: react that aryl sulfonyl chloride with p-toluidine to give final product.

Thus total steps: 1) amide formation (cinnamic acid + p-phenylenediamine) -> intermediate I. 2) chlorosulfonation of phenyl ring of intermediate I to introduce SO2Cl (maybe using chlorosulfonic acid). 3) sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine.

All leaves: cinnamic acid (commercial), p-phenylenediamine (commercial), p-toluidine (commercial), chlorosulfonic acid (reagent, not leaf). Leaves are commercially available chemicals, price likely low.

We need to verify templates for amide formation, chlorosulfonation, sulfonamide formation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for amide formation (functional_groups_formed: amide). Also for sulfonamide formation (functional_groups_formed: sulfonamides). Also for chlorosulfonation (functional_groups_formed: sulfonyl chloride? maybe "sulfonyl chloride" not in list; but we can treat as "sulfonyl chloride" not in list. Might be "sulfonyl chloride" not available. Could use "sulfonic" etc. Might be tricky.

But we can propose route without needing chlorosulfonation template; maybe we can use sulfonylation via sulfonyl chloride from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride reacting with phenyl A's amine? But phenyl A lacks amine. So not.

Alternative route: Use Suzuki coupling to attach phenyl A to sulfonyl phenyl after sulfonamide formation. Could be more steps.

Given time, we can propose route with three steps as described, assuming templates exist.

We need to produce JSON route. Need template IDs. We can search for amide formation template.
